reasoning: This insufficient-funds decline cannot be auto-resolved under any reading of policies.md:17, so the only live question is whether the retry budget is exhausted — and the policy contradicts itself there. With auto_retry_count=2, policies.md:13 ("up to 3 attempts total") says the budget is spent if the original charge counts as attempt one, while policies.md:16 ("escalate when the third retry fails") says a third retry is still owed. The case turns exactly on that difference, so it goes to a human; the customer is otherwise unremarkable (low risk, 11/12 successful payments, lifetime spend $1,847.50, below the $2,000 high-value bar at policies.md:88).

trace.rule: Insufficient funds — can auto-resolve: No; requires successful retry or human decision
trace.evidence: transaction.failure_reason is "insufficient_funds" and transaction.status is "failed"; the rule categorically forbids auto_resolve, leaving human_review or escalate.

auto_retry_count is 2. If the original charge counts toward the three, the budget is exhausted and this should escalate; if it does not, one retry remains. The policy does not define whether the initial attempt counts.

trace.rule: Escalate when: third retry fails, or customer contacts support
trace.evidence: Only 2 retries have occurred, so on a literal reading no third retry has failed and escalation is not triggered — directly at odds with the :13 reading that the 3-attempt budget is already spent. No field indicates the customer contacted support.

trace.rule: Retry timing: wait 2 days between retries
trace.evidence: Neither the issue payload nor the transaction record carries a timestamp for the last retry attempt (transaction has only created_at), and the payload has no days_since_purchase field, so retry spacing cannot be checked.

trace.rule: Customer notification: send after the second failed attempt
trace.evidence: auto_retry_count is 2, so the second-attempt threshold is reached and customer notification is due; this is a notification action, not a resolution path.

trace.rule: High-value customers (lifetime spend > $2000) get extra care / consider escalating
trace.evidence: customer.lifetime_spend is 1847.5, below the $2,000 threshold, so the high-value escalation nudge does not apply.

trace.rule: When in doubt, escalate — a human reviewing a borderline case costs less than a wrong automated decision
trace.evidence: The :13/:16 contradiction makes the retry-budget question undecidable from the document, so the case is routed to a human rather than guessed; escalate is reserved for the confirmed third-retry failure at :16, which has not been established.

dataGap: No timestamp for the most recent retry attempt is available (the transaction exposes only created_at, and the issue payload has no days_since_purchase), so the 2-days-between-retries rule at policies.md:14 could not be verified. Separately, policies.md is internally inconsistent for this case: :13 counts "3 attempts total" while :16 counts "three retries", and the document never says whether the original charge is attempt one — a human should settle that reading before this class of issue can be automated.
